title: How To Fix A Talkative Class
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin offers a multi-strategy plan for eliminating excessive classroom talking, arguing no single tactic suffices and that unwanted talking is usually the last symptom to resolve once broader classroom culture is cleaned up. He recommends tightening all other expectations first, explicitly defining and modeling what silence actually means, and explaining to students why silence benefits them so they buy in emotionally rather than merely comply. He also describes previewing talking expectations before each activity, teaching an optional nonverbal hand signal students can use to decline a peer's conversation without breaking silence, and enforcing violations immediately during the initial reset period to prove the new standard is real. He closes urging teachers to restart with authority if a class slips, without lecturing or showing frustration.
points: Argues unwanted talking is typically the last classroom issue to resolve and requires cleaning up broader expectations first.
Recommends explicitly defining, modeling, and having students practice what true classroom silence looks and sounds like.
Advises giving students the 'why' behind silence — framing sustained concentration as a lifelong success skill — to build buy-in.
Describes an optional hand-signal strategy students can use to decline a peer's attempt at conversation without breaking the rule.
Recommends immediate, vigilant enforcement in the early reset period to prove the new no-talking standard is genuinely in force.
quotes: The truth is, you can fix excessive and impermissible talking and expect silence whenever you need it.
You must change the culture of sloppiness and carelessness first before you can expect to rid your classroom of chattiness, side-whispering, and the like.
There must be complete understanding of what silence is according to your definition before you can ask them to replicate it.
They need to know that the ability to concentrate for long periods of time is a critical success skill that is key to their learning, their progress, and their very future.
They’re not allowed to speak to the offending party, look at them, or make any other gesture. They just hold up their signal and continue working.
Restore respect for you and every student in the class by defending their right to learn and enjoy school without interference .
